name: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum
charge: Not repenting after the mighty works done in them
summary: Most of Christ's miracles were done in three towns on the north shore of Galilee, and they did not repent. He measured them against Tyre, Sidon and Sodom and found them worse off in the judgment, because more had been shown them. Capernaum, exalted unto heaven, was to be brought down to hell.
offense: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not. If the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. Capernaum had heard the sermon in the synagogue, seen the centurion's servant healed and the paralytic carried down through the roof, and stayed as it was.
judgment: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you. And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

entries.commentary: John hears in the prison the works of Christ and sends two of his disciples to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? The messiah was spoken of from Genesis forward. They knew he was coming and they knew the description given of him.

Christ answers by pointing to the works: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. He is quoting Isaiah back to them.
Blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

What went ye out into the wilderness to see? Not a reed shaken with the wind, nor a man in soft clothing, but a prophet, and more than a prophet. John is the messenger written of, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way.
Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist, notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom in view is Israel. The violence is what was done to them, and it is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed.
All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

That generation is likened to children in the markets who piped and were not danced to. Christ did not move to the beat of their drum. John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking and they called him a gluttonous man. Nothing would have satisfied them.

Woe unto Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, because the mighty works were done among them and they repented not. Tyre, Sidon and Sodom would have repented at what these cities saw. Men watched works no ordinary man could do and still would not turn.
These things are hid from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. No man knoweth the Father save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

The Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place whither he himself would come. The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.
Behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves. Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

Into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house, and if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it. In the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

Heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you. That word is said to a house that received them. Where there is charity and brotherhood enough to take a labourer in, the kingdom is near to that house.
Where they are not received, they wipe off the very dust of the city, and it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! If the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. Other nations would have turned at what Israel watched and did not turn at. That is what a stiffnecked people looks like. He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

The seventy return with joy that even the devils are subject unto them, and he answers, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

I thank thee, O Father, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes. No man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him. A man does not know the Father apart from the son.

Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see. Many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them. The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them.

A lawyer stands up and asks what he shall do to inherit eternal life, and is sent to the law: What is written in the law? how readest thou? Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and thy neighbour as thyself. Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

Willing to justify himself, he asks, And who is my neighbour? A priest and a Levite pass by on the other side. Both were of the southern kingdom, and neither had mercy on their own. A Samaritan had compassion, bound up his wounds, and paid for his keeping. Samaria was the head of Ephraim, so the man who showed mercy was of the northern kingdom. Go, and do thou likewise. The mercy that was withheld between the two houses is the very thing commanded here.

Martha was cumbered about much serving and asked that Mary be told to help her; Mary sat at his feet and heard his word. Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her. A man can be so taken up with the business of the day that the word never gets in him.

Christ is led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted, and after forty days and forty nights of fasting he is an hungred. The tempter comes at the weakest point and goes at the flesh first: command that these stones be made bread. This is the same set of temptations the man and the woman met in the garden, and they run through everything the enemy uses.

Christ answers with what is written: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. The formula is given here. The flesh is weak and profits nothing; the spirit is strengthened by the word, and that is how the temptation is endured.

The devil sets him on a pinnacle of the temple and quotes scripture at him. Satan knows the scriptures and will use them. This is why brothers and sisters must be able to try what is brought to them. Men can come with fringes and strong classes and still be workers of deceit.
Christ answers again with the law: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. He fights the enemy with the commandments, which is what those who say the law is done away have thrown away.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world and offers them for worship. This is the pride of life and the lust of the eyes, offered to a man who at that moment was a carpenter out of Nazareth. Christ answers a third time out of the law: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
The devil leaves him and angels come and minister unto him. The leaving is not permanent.

John is cast into prison and Christ departs into Galilee, and dwells in Capernaum in the borders of Zebulun and Nephthalim. The scripture calls that country Galilee of the Gentiles. Zebulun and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and this is the key to who the gentiles are that the gospel goes to after the southern kingdom rejects it.
From that time Christ begins to preach the same word John preached: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. The fishers come first; the hunters come after. Peter and Andrew straightway left their nets. That was their living, and they left it without hesitation. Many in this truth have been in it for years and know little, because they were not willing to give up what they were building.
James and John immediately left the ship and their father and followed him. That is faith, and the Most High uses men who will make that kind of sacrifice.
He goes about all Galilee teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness, and great multitudes follow him.

verses.text: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:
Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:
That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin.
He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
